pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.sentence: Every failure record of a ticket's phase becomes exactly one attempt record n plus 1 with a backoff of min(10 s x 2^(n-1), 5 min), or, after the third attempt, exactly one dead record that maps to owner-acts so the owner sees one card, and nothing loops and nothing is silent.
purpose.is: The one owner of retry in the factory: no seat, no script and no other node decides whether to try again (RC2: no system-owned retry; D01 B: bounded retry with backoff and one escalation record).
A table, not a judgement: the failure kind names the phase and role of the next attempt; the arithmetic is a pure function of n (Symphony SPEC.md lines 797 to 801; SPEC-16.D d-backoff-pure).
purpose.is-not: Not a re-prompt of the same seat: a retry is a fresh one-shot seat with the failure record attached (plan failure-cases bad-output: a fresh seat retries with the failure attached, never the seat that failed).

Not an architect hop: the third failure used to route as 423 to the architect for a split or re-scope (SPEC-03 s-retry); here it is a dead record and one owner card, because the architect lane is retired into cards (D11, D12).
purpose.decisions: D01, D02 (C36), D11 (C39), D12 (C40), D17 (C49), T02, V17 (standing policies carry the dead card's default).

record.field: seat.result blocked 423 with its terminal_reason (N-15: a seat result is done 200 or blocked 423, never anything else; a dead run yields blocked with terminal_reason crashed or no_result); phase.failed 423 (N-15 and N-19: the phase's structured output was rejected); review.changes 422 (N-19); merge.conflict 409 and merge.failed 500 (N-09); stall 500 (N-12); validator.refused 412 and validator.failed 423 (N-18); gate.verdict red 422 or missing 500 (N-08); dispatch.refused 412 (N-07).

The ticket and the phase and attempt that failed; attempt comes from the dispatch the run belonged to (1 to 3), or 0 for a failure before any dispatch (dispatch.refused, gate missing on a first head).
The run that failed, when there was one (N-15 names it run_id); N-01 already refused a stale token, so a failure record here is from the live run.
The failure's own fields: review findings, red suites and gate url, conflict base, stall reason, the failing acceptance command; copied into the next attempt's brief by N-13.

input.starts-when: A failure record is committed. Level-triggered as well: the scheduler tick lists failure records with no attempt or dead record naming them (handled_by empty) and starts a traversal for each, so a lost traversal is caught within one tick.

record.field: ticket, colon, phase, colon, n plus 1; one per attempt, ever.
The next attempt: attempt equals n plus 1 (2 or 3); phase and role from the retry table.

UTC second equal to now plus backoff plus jitter: backoff is min(10 x 2^(n-1), 300) seconds; jitter is a uniform fraction in plus or minus 0.2 of the backoff (scheduler.json retry.jitter 0.2, L01 section 6), passed in by the caller so tests pass zero.
The record this attempt answers; N-13 puts it in the brief.
ticket, colon, phase, colon, dead; one per ticket and phase, ever.
The three attempts with their failure ids and kinds, so the card reads once (SPEC-17 1.1.0 draft s-chain rule of climbing: the lower link attaches what it tried).
true; the status code map maps dead to owner-acts and N-28 posts exactly one card keyed by this record id.
From the retry table per failure kind: split the ticket, re-scope, system-lane fault, or leave dead; the card's recommended option, so a yes is one word (memory no-bureaucracy-creep).
The standing policy row for the failure kind, when one exists (V17): what happens if the owner does not answer by the deadline, applied by N-29's rule, so nothing waits for ever.

output.ends-when: The failure record's handled_by field is set to the attempt or dead record id by compare-and-swap; the traversal is over. The attempt re-enters N-02 as a fresh claim with attempt n plus 1 and not_before (dag.md section 4).

mechanism.where: Go package retry inside the service; Next(failure, history, now, jitterFraction, table) returns an attempt or dead intent; the engine writes it and compare-and-swaps the failure's handled_by.
mechanism.step: Compare-and-swap the failure record's handled_by from empty to this traversal's id with its generation. Refused: another traversal has it; end.

Load every attempt and dead record for the ticket and phase. n equals the failed attempt number (the dispatch's attempt; for a failure before dispatch, the count of attempt records plus the first implicit one).
Look up the failure kind in the retry table (config retry.json, validated by schema; values below are the defaults and every one is a key):

row.attach: seat.result (the question or observation the seat posted as blocked)
row.policy: POL-blocked-land-it (factory/config/policies.json), deadline 1800 s, default: land on the criteria as written

seat.result blocked 423, terminal_reason killed_stall, killed_deadline, killed_lease_lost

row.failure: seat.result blocked 423, terminal_reason crashed, no_result, bundle_mismatch
row.attach: the launcher's terminal reason and stderr_path
the rejected structured output and the validation error

row.failure: validator.failed 500 (the validator itself failed: store, workspace, podman, image)
row.next-phase: none: N-18's controller retries the same set on its next tick, up to 3 (nodes/N-18/spec.xml#retries); no seat is dispatched, because the validator is code, never a seat

row.attach: the review findings and the head sha
row.note: the reviewer's attempt counter is not spent; the worker's is (SPEC-03 s-retry: attempt counts a seat's tries on one ticket; routes.json row 7)

row.attach: merge-main instruction with base sha (routes.json row 10; PR 35 S2-078)
row.recommendation: rebase by hand is never needed; a third conflict is a scheduling defect (memory one-file-one-in-flight-ticket)

row.attach: the stall record (reason, last heartbeat age)
row.recommendation: split the ticket or raise the role's stall bound

row.next-phase: spec (attempt n+1 on the same cut-request key)
row.attach: the failing acceptance command and its exit code
row.recommendation: the design anchor is wrong or the command needs a fixture

row.next-role: gate (code: re-post pr.opened for the head)

row.recommendation: files-claimed: wait for the other ticket (no attempt is spent, see N-07 retries); role-unknown or brief-missing: system-lane fault

mechanism.step: If n is below 3: write attempt n plus 1 with not_before now plus backoff(n) plus jitter. If n equals 3: write dead with the three failure ids and the recommendation and policy from the table.

A dispatch.refused with reason files-claimed charges no attempt: the failure is handled by marking it with the next tick's re-examination (N-07 step 6 sees the lease again) and no attempt record is written; this is the one row with next-phase same and no attempt spent, so a ticket blocked by another's files cannot die of it.

Fix tickets cut from N-10's fix-for-hold ticket.request (a spec-phase cut request, nodes/N-03/spec.xml#input) count their attempts here like any ticket; the count of fix tickets per hold is N-10's own (three fix tickets), so the bound on a red main is three tickets of up to three attempts each per phase, every one a record.

Compare-and-swap the failure's handled_by from this traversal's id to the written record id. The attempt record is N-02's input: it grants a lease with attempt n plus 1, not_before and a new fencing token; N-07 dispatches it when not_before has passed.
mechanism.invariant: One attempt record per (ticket, phase, n plus 1), one dead per (ticket, phase); never a fourth attempt (K10: limits are fields the system enforces, not prose the model counts).

backoff(n) equals min(10 x 2^(n-1), 300) seconds: 10 s after attempt 1, 20 s after attempt 2; the cap of 300 s is reached only for n at or above 6, which cannot occur, and stays in the formula so the table and the field's reference agree.
mechanism.diagram: flowchart TD F["failure record (kind, ticket, phase, attempt n)"] --> C{"CAS handled_by empty to mine?"} C -- refused --> E["another traversal has it, end"] C -- ok --> T["retry table row for the kind"] T --> NC{"files-claimed?"} NC -- yes --> Z["no attempt spent; next tick re-examines"] NC -- no --> N{"n below 3?"} N -- yes --> A["attempt n+1, not_before = now + min(10 x 2^(n-1), 300) s +/- 20%"] N -- no --> D["dead 500: three failures attached, recommendation, policy default"] A --> N02["N-02 fresh claim with attempt n+1"] D --> N28["N-28 exactly one card"] D --> N41["N-41 alerts"] A --> W["CAS handled_by to the record id"] D --> W

start.sentence: Nothing here starts by an agent typing.
start.by: The commit of a failure record starts a traversal; the scheduler tick (N-07) lists unhandled failure records every tick and starts the missing traversals, so no failure is forgotten after a crash or a lost commit event.
start.restart: After a crash a traversal that claimed handled_by and died leaves a claim older than retry.claim_seconds (default 60); the tick resets it to empty by compare-and-swap on generation and the traversal runs again; the idempotency keys make a half-written attempt a 409 that is read back.

wait.fallback: end; the next tick retries; three in a row write store.unreachable 500 once
retry 1 s, 2 s, 4 s; then the claim is released and the next tick retries; retry.write.failed 500 once per failure id

wait.on: not_before passing before N-07 dispatches attempt n plus 1
wait.fallback: none needed: the wait is a timestamp N-07 compares, not a sleep; a service restart loses nothing because not_before is in the store

wait.on: the owner answering a dead card
wait.timeout: the standing policy's deadline when the failure kind has a row (1800 s for blocked), else none
wait.fallback: the policy default is applied by N-29's rule and recorded as a ruling; a kind with no row stays dead and the card stays up, which is the owner's own choice (policies.json: a kind with no row waits for its answer without end; the card is on the page, not a cog in the line, because the ticket is dead and the line runs on)

waits.rule: No sleep in this node; every backoff is a not_before timestamp.

step.name: claim and write
step.then: retry.write.failed 500 once per failure id; the next tick re-runs the traversal

retries.not-retried: A dead record is never retried by the system; only an owner ruling (N-29) that unblocks the ticket re-enters it at N-03 with attempt reset to 1 and a new phase traversal (dag.md section 4 re-entry from N-29); the Scheduler.Retry RPC of scheduler.proto is that ruling's mechanism and is never called by a seat.
retries.report: Every then clause is a record; the dead record carries the whole history so the card is one read.

many-agents.readers: Any seat reads attempt and dead records; a brief for attempt n plus 1 carries the failure record by id so the fresh seat reads what the last one hit.
many-agents.two-traversals: Two traversals for one failure (a commit event and a tick) both compare-and-swap handled_by; one wins; the loser ends. If the winner dies, the claim ages out and the tick re-runs it; a second attempt record cannot appear because the key ticket:phase:n+1 exists (409, read back).
many-agents.two-failures: Two failure records for one attempt (a stall and the launcher's seat.result blocked killed_stall for the same run, or a review.changes and a gate red on the same head) each start a traversal; the first writes attempt n plus 1 and the second finds the key taken, reads it back and sets its own handled_by to that record, so one attempt answers both, which is right: one fresh seat gets both failures in its brief (N-13 attaches every failure the attempt handled).
many-agents.fresh-seat: A retry never resumes the failed seat's session: it is a fresh one-shot run with a fresh workspace (N-14) and the failure attached; a resumed session would carry the context that failed (K02).
many-agents.conflict-reports: Every refused compare-and-swap and every 409 is logged with the key and counted; never a silent overwrite.
many-agents.test: Test case two-failures-one-attempt: a stall and a review.changes on one attempt write one attempt record and both failures point at it (checklist c-two-failures).

emits.acts: N-02 grants the next lease; N-07 dispatches when not_before passes
owner-acts: N-28 one card; N-41 alerts; N-29's ruling is the only way back

state-paths.root: $COQ_STATE as in ../N-07/spec.xml#state-paths; path elements in N-45's generator form.
state-paths.path: Rows: attempt and dead records; the handled_by field of failure records. Dead records of tickets with no ruling are never pruned; attempts prune after the ticket's verified record and retention (N-01's row).
One line per decision with n, backoff and the key.

permissions.reads: failure records of the kinds listed, attempt and dead history, the retry table, the policies table.
permissions.writes: attempt, dead, retry.write.failed, store.unreachable records; the handled_by field of failure records by compare-and-swap; the retry log.
permissions.never: No seat start (N-07 and N-15 do that), no prompt, no pane, no GitHub, no edit of attempt or dead records once written.
permissions.seat: No seat can write attempt or dead (N-01 writer identity); a seat that wants another try posts its result and leaves; the system decides.

runbook.bring-up: factory/config/retry.json present and lint-green; set retry.enabled true; proof: a failure record with handled_by set and its attempt record.
runbook.read-status: Scheduler.Status lists attempts waiting with their not_before, dead tickets with their recommendation and whether a card is up; the Alerts screen shows dead_open.
runbook.unblock-dead: Only a ruling on the card (N-29) moves a dead ticket; the Scheduler.Retry RPC runs under that ruling's id and never by hand.
runbook.change-a-bound: Edit factory/config/retry.json through a ticket; Scheduler.Reload loads it; no restart.
runbook.registry: Generated into shared/cleanup-registry.json from the state-paths element (../N-45/spec.xml#state-paths).
